wilcoxon.min_achievable_p_note: With 5 folds the minimum two-sided Wilcoxon p is 0.0625; it CANNOT reach p<0.05, so this test cannot establish significance regardless of the effect.

CRITICAL_INTERPRETATION_for_authors.issue: McNemar tests thresholded ACCURACY, not ranking (AUC). Celeb-DF sealed test is 83.6% fake, so predict-all-fake accuracy = 0.836.
CRITICAL_INTERPRETATION_for_authors.celebdf_prism_vs_xception: PRISM @theta=0.5 has real-recall 0.183 (predicts fake for ~82% of reals) -> accuracy 0.834 ~= fake prevalence. Xception has real-recall 0.836 (genuinely detects reals) but pays an accuracy penalty on the imbalanced set -> accuracy 0.713. Thus McNemar shows PRISM higher-accuracy on Celeb-DF, but this is a CLASS-IMBALANCE / THRESHOLD ARTIFACT, NOT better detection. By AUC (ranking): Xception 0.825 vs PRISM 0.717 (Wilcoxon folds; locked DeLong z=15.4, p<1e-16) -> Xception ranks substantially better cross-dataset. DO NOT present the Celeb-DF McNemar as PRISM winning.
CRITICAL_INTERPRETATION_for_authors.ffpp_prism_vs_xception: Xception significantly better (McNemar p<1e-13 AND AUC 0.990 vs 0.842) -> unambiguous, report plainly.
CRITICAL_INTERPRETATION_for_authors.196_vs_50_53: The genuine 196-D representation gain is a RANKING (AUC) effect: DeLong 196-vs-53 p=2.2e-9, 196-vs-50 p=1.7e-6 (already reported). On McNemar ACCURACY it shows 196>53 significant (theta p=1e-11) but 196-vs-50 NOT significant (p=0.25/0.75), because at fixed thresholds on the 84%-fake set both are near predict-all-fake. Report the AUC/DeLong result as the representation evidence; McNemar accuracy is threshold-dependent.
CRITICAL_INTERPRETATION_for_authors.AUTHORS: [AUTHORS: reconcile the accuracy(McNemar) vs ranking(AUC/DeLong) divergence in framing; the paper reports AUC, on which Xception leads cross-dataset and 196-D leads over 50/53-D.]
